paper.title: Data Poisoning Attacks on Stochastic Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Online attack system model (reward poisoning of stochastic bandits)
unmapped: The 'learner' analysed is an attacker that observes (a_t, r_t) and adds a perturbation eps_t to the reward fed to an unknown bandit algorithm with O(log T) regret
Objective: force the bandit algorithm to pull a suboptimal target arm a* T-o(T) times while minimizing l1 attack cost sum_t |eps_t|
learner_knows refers to the attacker's knowledge (sigma, K, delta)
settings.definition_quote: The attacker stealthily monitors the decision of the bandit algorithm $a_t$ at each time $t$ and poisons the reward signal returned from the bandit environment by equation (\ref{eqn:poison}). Then the bandit algorithm receives the manipulated reward signal $r'_t$ and updates unaware of the attacker.

symbols.sum_nontarget: sum over arms a different from the target arm a*
symbols.mu_target: mean reward of the target arm a*
symbols.beta_1: beta(1) = sqrt(2 sigma^2 log(pi^2 K/(3 delta)))

conditions: the bandit algorithm achieves O(log T) regret with probability at least 1-delta
tuning: confidence parameter delta used in beta(n)

source.label: thm:adaptive
source.quote: Given any $\delta\in(0,0.5)$, assume that the bandit algorithm achieves an $O(\log T)$ regret bound with probability at least $1-\delta$. With probability at least $1-2\delta$, the ACE attacker forces the bandit algorithm to play the target arm $a^*$ in $N_{a^*}(T)$ times, such that $N_{a^*}(T) = T-o(T)$, ... In particular, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, the ACE attack is successful and the accumulated attack cost is $\sum_{t=1}^T|\epsilon_t| \leq O(\sum_{a\not= a^*}([\mu_a-\mu_{a^*}]^+ + 4\beta(1)) \log T)$.

results.notes: Bound on the attacker's cumulative l1 attack cost (not regret), holding w.p. >= 1-2delta; also guarantees N_{a*}(T)=T-o(T), i.e. linear regret for the victim. Theorem also gives a per-round cost bound.

symbols.sum_nontarget: sum over arms a different from the target arm a*
symbols.C_a: constant attack magnitude for arm a

conditions: the bandit algorithm achieves O(log T) regret
C_a > [mu_a - mu_{a*}]^+ for all a != a*

source.label: prop:constant
source.quote:
Assume that the bandit algorithm achieves an $O(\log T)$ regret bound. Then the constant attack with $\{C_a\}_{a
ot=a^*}$ succeeds if and only if $C_a > [\mu_{a}-\mu_{a^*}]^+$, $ orall a 
ot= a^*$. If the attack succeeds, then the expected attack cost is $O(\sum_{a
ot= a^*}C_a\log T)$.

results.notes: Expected attack cost of the oracle constant attack; quantity is attack cost, not regret.

cited_results.setting_description: Online reward-poisoning attack on a stochastic bandit algorithm with O(log T) regret; attacker knows the means; expected attack cost
